HARD v1 Table 1 static HARD-Both ASRs 12.1/1.3/13.9/7.4 conflict with introduction/adjacent prose 15.4/1.0/6.7/10.2; appendix MC/SP UA 86.3/92.0 conflicts with Table 1 85.9/95.1. Table 3's GLM-5.2 memory-contamination row independently matches Table 1 on ASR=13.9 and UA=85.9, partially favoring that lineage without resolving all static cells. LPA 4.8 vs 12.1 and GPT-5.5 UA=7.2 are verified within their exact five-round regimes.

Table 4 values are verified and w/o CBR is explicitly episodic-memory-disabled, yet it rises 78.65→84.47 (+5.82pp), slightly more than the two CBR arms. The paper-era repository lacks the five-iteration experiment harness/CBR implementation and v2 does not specify the no-CBR inter-iteration operator, seeds/order, retry/cumulative accounting or raw manifests. Therefore same-iteration CBR separation is usable, but the shared upward iteration slope is causally unidentified and must not be attributed specifically to memory learning.

ViT-t/ImageNet subset-size results and reward-std declines are verified: fullset 65.23/71.09/73.47/75.34 for 1/1024→1/128 and declines 0.06/0.06/0.08/0.13. The 0.2/0.1 thresholds are empirical Rocket diagnostics, not general constants or a direct rank-correlation test. The approximately-80x claim is a separate ResNet-18/ImageNet EFLOPs comparison (9.7e2 vs 1.2e1), not direct wall-clock speedup. No raw ImageNet subset/full paired-rank artifact is explicitly listed in the released data inventory.

The v4 formal theorem gives interval tracking error <=(Lambda+2eta)/(eta L), so O(1/sqrt(T)) applies to the full horizon with eta=T^-1/2 and constant Lambda, not uniformly to every short interval. Theorem 2 verifies O((Cmax/(1-phi))*sqrt(nT log(nT))) expected stochastic cost regret; scalar-threshold and interval corollaries are tilde-O(T^(2/3)) and tilde-O(T^(3/4)). Projection adds residual accounting that can hide linear debt, and Lemma 1 gives a concrete linear-validity-failure instance. Guaranteed-success/failure boundary arms are structural assumptions used to bound the unprojected state and prove both validity and efficiency; they are not merely implementation preferences, though the paper does not prove they are the unique possible stabilizer.

The paper verifies a random pooled manual sample of n=50 with estimated ~12% heuristic-judge misclassification, mostly ambiguous-redirection false negatives, and no false positives observed. It does not report a class-conditional denominator/confusion matrix, confidence interval, inter-rater/annotation protocol, or controlled corruption sweep, so the observation is not a calibrated error model and does not establish zero true false-positive probability. Appendix Table 2 also gives only 20 generations for Devstral. A separate provenance inconsistency remains: method text/Algorithm 1 describe {0,.4,1} while Appendix/results use a .8 band and the linked public HeuristicJudge snapshot scores detected compliance at .8.
